./docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:974:`kill` does **not** flip a cancellation token in a running deadreckon process. If a deadreckon `run` is still running, `kill` only signals its child PIDs; the deadreckon process itself relies on its own cancellation token tree, which `kill` doesn't reach across processes. # Child Summary: Scaffold project + 3D world

Plan: aa20e56506a548d8ba4bece648c55b26
Task: task-0
Role: Child
Provider: cli:codex
Run: 0117a88149604a6e8af1b8f6e2ffc808
Status: completed

Library: /Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/task-0-0a447a6b/0117a88149604a6e8af1b8f6e2ffc808

## Goal

Create the initial project scaffold for a browser-based multiplayer flight simulator using Three.js and Vite. Initialize package.json with dependencies: three, vite, cannon-es (physics), socket.io-client, and dat.gui. Create directory structure: /src (client code), /server (Node.js server), /assets (models, textures, audio), /public. Implement src/main.js that boots a Three.js scene with: a perspective camera, WebGL renderer attached to a full-window canvas, ambient + directional sun lighting, a procedurally generated tessellated terrain mesh (use a PlaneGeometry subdivided 256x256 with simplex/perlin noise heightmap for mountains/valleys), a skybox or sky shader with atmospheric scattering, and a simple placeholder airplane mesh (box + wings) parented to a control rig. Add an animation loop using requestAnimationFrame. Acceptance: `npm install && npm run dev` opens a browser showing a tessellated terrain with a placeholder plane visible, camera in chase position, 60fps on desktop. Files to create: package.json, vite.config.js, index.html, src/main.js, src/world/terrain.js, src/world/sky.js, src/entities/airplane.js. Use ES modules. No multiplayer or physics yet — just a rendered world with a plane.

**Current Role Behavior**

`PlanRole::Child` and `PlanRole::Coder`:
They launch with `deadreckon run --from <source_dir>`. Today `<source_dir>` is always `plan.parent_cwd` or the fork process cwd, regardless of `depends_on`.

`PlanRole::Reviewer`:
`plan_child_source_dir` tries the first dependency’s completed run, preferring its promoted library dir, falling back to `state.working_dir`. Then `run_plan_child` uses `deadreckon extend <parent-run-id> ...`, via `review_parent_run_id`.

[main.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:9428)

So review-mode gets lineage and artifact inheritance; full-plan dependencies only get prompt context.
